Merge Behaviors

Merge is a core pipeline stage responsible for combining the current committed FeatureCell state with a newly resolved pipeline value. The Merge stage defines how incoming values are structurally integrated into state before any downstream processing occurs.

Merge operates after resolution and before operators, filters, reducers, and taps. It produces a single merged candidate value that represents the authoritative state input for the remainder of the pipeline execution.

Merge Stage

The Merge Stage combines the existing FeatureCell state with the resolved incoming value produced by the Resolve stage. Its responsibility is limited to determining how the two values are structurally combined into a single candidate state value.

Merge behaviors do not perform business logic, conditional evaluation, or policy decisions. They do not transform values based on rules or intent. Instead, they define the structural semantics of state combination—such as replacement, preservation, or composition—between the current state and the incoming value.

Exactly one Merge behavior participates in pipeline execution for a FeatureCell. The Merge stage always produces a single merged result, which is then forwarded to downstream stages for further evaluation. If the merge result represents a cleared state, that outcome is propagated as the authoritative merge result for the current execution.

The Merge Stage does not emit snapshots, does not mutate existing state directly, and does not influence pipeline scheduling or control flow. Its sole responsibility is to compute the merged candidate value that downstream stages may accept, modify, or suppress.

Core Pipeline Stage

The Merge stage is a core pipeline stage and is always present as part of the FeatureCell lifecycle. Every pipeline execution includes exactly one active merge strategy to combine the current committed state with the resolved incoming value.

When no merge behavior is explicitly provided, the pipeline automatically applies the default withArrayMerge behavior. This ensures that merge semantics are always defined and that state combination produces a predictable, immutable result for downstream stages.

FeatureCells may replace the default merge strategy by supplying a custom or pre-built merge behavior as part of the provideFeatureCell definition. Merge behaviors are declared declaratively and participate directly in pipeline execution, allowing state-combination semantics to be customized without altering downstream operators, filters, reducers, or taps.

Exactly one merge behavior may be active per FeatureCell. If multiple merge behaviors are provided, pipeline initialization fails to prevent ambiguous or conflicting state combination rules.

Note

The Merge stage is entered exclusively through explicit state-update APIs. Pipeline executions that invoke merge semantics are initiated via the mergeState method, which supply the incoming value and optional merge configuration used by the active Merge behavior.

Diagrams
Available Array Merge Behaviors

Array merge behaviors define how list-based state values are combined during the Merge stage. These behaviors treat arrays as immutable values and always return a new array instance when a merge occurs.

Available Object Merge Behaviors

Object merge behaviors define how structured, object-based state values are combined during the Merge stage. These behaviors treat objects as immutable values and always return a new object when a merge occurs.

Object merge strategies differ in how deeply they combine nested structures. Shallow merge replaces properties at the first level only, while deep merge recursively merges nested plain objects.

Configuration

Merge behaviors may optionally be influenced by the clearUndefined configuration flag. When clearUndefined is enabled, an incoming undefined value is treated as an intentional clear request and results in the FeatureCell state being cleared. When disabled, incoming undefined values preserve the existing state and produce no structural change.

The clearUndefined option is supplied at the time a merge-style update is initiated and is evaluated by the active merge behavior during the Merge stage. It does not affect resolution, operators, or downstream pipeline stages.
